questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

A large swarm of dogs was blocking the way.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - pack of​.

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the marked option:
    • pack- a group of wild animals, especially wolves or dogs, living and hunting together
  • Let's look at the meanings of the other given options: 
    • swarm- a large or dense group of insects, especially flying ones
    • herd- a large group of animals, especially hoofed mammals, that live, feed, or migrate together or are kept together as livestock
    • school- a large group of fish or sea mammals
  • Hence, from the given meanings, we find that pack is the correct collective noun for 'dogs'.
     

Correct sentence: A large pack of dogs was blocking the way.

Additional Information

  • Collective nouns take a singular verb with them.
  • For example:
    • The herd of cows are grazing in the farms.
    • The herd of cows is grazing in the farms.​
  • If there is a division among the members of the collective noun, a plural verb and plural pronoun are used.
  • Example:
    • The audience have been arguing inside the theatre for an hour.

questions.question: Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'. Anurag asked me why didn't you pay the driver.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Anurag asked me why didn't you pay the driver.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is- 'I didn't pay.'

Key Points

  • We can use why in indirect questions:
  • Structure: ....... why + Subject + verb .........
    • Example: I wonder why he told nobody he was getting married.
  • Therefore, the use of 'didn't you pay' should be replaced by 'I didn't pay' to make it grammatically correct.
  • Correct sentence: Anurag asked me why I didn't pay the driver.

Additional Information 

  • Countable nouns, as the term suggests, refer to things that can be counted. 
  • They have singular and plural forms.
    • Example: table, tables; month, months; pen, pens.
  • Uncountable nouns cannot be counted.
  • They have a singular form and do not have a plural form.
    • Example: dirt, rice, information, furniture, and hair.

Hinglish 

  • हम Indirect questions में क्यों का उपयोग कर सकते हैं:
  • Structure: ....... why + Subject + verb .........
    • Example: I wonder why he told nobody he was getting married.
  • इसलिए वाक्य में 'didn't you pay' के प्रयोग को 'I didn't pay' से बदल देना चाहिए ताकि वह व्याकरण की दृष्टि से सही हो।​

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

questions.question: Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. There will be little more pupils in the class next year, but we have enough space.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

There will be little more pupils in the class next year, but we have enough space.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'a few more.'

Key Points

  • In the underlined segment, the use of the quantifier 'little' is incorrect.
  • The quantifier 'little' means not much or not enough.
  • The quantifier 'little' is used with uncountable nouns.
  • The given sentence is talking about a spacious classroom capable of accomodating some more pupils next year.
  • In the given sentence the noun 'pupils' is a plural countable noun.
  • Therefore, the quantifier ''a few'' should be used in place of the quantifier 'little'.
  • The quantifier ''a few'' is used with plural countable nouns.
  • The quantifier ''a few'' means somewhat (though not much). It has a positive meaning. It is used in the context of 'some.'
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Sentence: There will be a few more pupils in the class next year, but we have enough space.

Additional Information

  • The quantifier 'much' is used with uncountable nouns, mainly in negative sentences and questions, or after as, how, so, too; a large amount of something. (किसी वस्‍तु की अधिक मात्रा)
  • The quantifier 'few' is used with plural countable nouns but it means limited or below average; hardly any. It has a negative meaning. (सीमित या औसत से कम; शायद ही कोई)
  • The quantifier 'a little' is used with singular uncountable nouns and it means a small amount of something. (किसी वस्‍तु की थोड़ी मात्रा, थोड़ी-सी)
     

Hinglish

  • रेखांकित खण्ड में quantifier 'little' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • Quantifier 'little' का अर्थ "अधिक या पर्याप्त नहीं" होता है।
  • Quantifier 'little' का प्रयोग uncountable nouns के साथ किया जाता है।
  • दिया गया वाक्य एक विशाल कक्षा के बारे में बात कर रहा है जो अगले साल कुछ और विद्यार्थियों को समायोजित करने में सक्षम है।
  • दिए गए वाक्य में noun 'pupils' एक plural countable noun है।
  • इसलिए quantifier 'little' के स्थान पर quantifier ''a few'' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • Quantifier ''a few'' का प्रयोग plural countable nouns के साथ किया जाता है।
  • Quantifier ''a few'' का अर्थ है एक छोटी संख्या; कुछ; कुछ हद तक (हालांकि ज्यादा नहीं)। इसका सकारात्मक अर्थ है। इसका प्रयोग 'some' के संदर्भ में किया जाता है।
     

अत: सही उत्तर विकल्प 2 है।

सही वाक्य: There will be a few more pupils in the class next year, but we have enough space.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good in the individual , the society, the country and the world.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good in the individual, the society, the country and the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2 – "good of the individual".
 
Key Points
  • The phrase "for the good of" is a standard idiomatic expression meaning for the benefit or welfare of someone or something.
  • In the sentence, the intended meaning is that education serves the benefit of various entities — the individual, society, the country, and the world.
  • Hence, the correct structure is: "for the good of the individual", not “for the good for/on/by.”
  • “Good of” is always used with reference to a beneficiary, and is commonly seen in expressions like “for the good of mankind” or “for the good of the community.”
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2 – "good of the individual".
 
Correct Sentence: "Universal high-quality education is the best way forward for developing and maximising our country's rich talents and resources for the good of the individual, the society, the country and the world."
 
Additional Information
  • The expression “for the good of” is a fixed phrase in English and should not be altered unless the meaning or grammatical structure demands it.
  • Other prepositions like “for,” “on,” or “by” after “good” would either change the meaning or render the phrase grammatically incorrect in this context.
  • This phrase is widely used in academic, legal, and social discourse to indicate collective or individual benefit.

The correct sentence is- A school teacher earns a lower salary than a college lecturer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’. There was a bell over the door that jingled whenever a customer entered
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

There was a bell over the door that jingled whenever a customer entered
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Option 4".
Key Points
  • In the given sentence, there is a connection between a noun 'a bell' and a clause 'jingled whenever a customer entered'.
    • 'Relative pronoun - that' is always used to connect a clause or phrase with people or things.
The given sentence is accurate, so there is no substitution required.
Important Points
  • in 'Option 1 - which jingled wherever', a wrong conjunction 'wherever' can be seen that makes no sense with the given sentence,
  • In 'Option 2 - who jingles whenever', an incorrect relative pronoun 'who' can be seen that is used for people only, not for the object like a bell.
  • In 'Option 3 - that jingle when', we can see the wrong usage of tense 'jingle' and conjunction 'when', whereas the given sentence is in the past tense.
Based on above points, No substitution is required.
Additional Information
  • Relative pronouns like 'Who' or 'Which'  always connect a clause or phrase to a noun or pronoun.
  • 'Who' is always used for people. For example, I know the person who lives here.
  • 'Which' is always used for objects & animals. For example, My mobile, which I bought last week, is lost.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. She walked among me without greeting me.
questions.questionHtml:

She walked among me without greeting me.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'past me'. 

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
  • The erroneous Part 'among me' should be 'past me'. 
  • Here, in the given question 'walked past me' is the correct usage because "Walk past" means to change your position in relation to something, by walking. So basically there is an object that you pass as you walk. So you walk past it and it is then behind you.
  • And the structure of it is "verb + adverb particle, in this case, walk past."
  • Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is Option 4. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: She walked past me without greeting me. 

Mistake Points

  • We tend to confuse ourselves between 'walked passed' and 'walked past'. 
  • In this case, 'past' is correctly being used.
  • The verb in this sentence is walked and 'past' is acting as an adverb.
  • A good rule to keep track of troublesome sentences like these is that if a verb indicating motion is already in your sentence, we will always couple it with 'past' not 'passed'. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
